html:
Christopher Columbus was a navigator from Genoa who sailed west across the Atlantic for the Spanish crown in 1492 and reached the Caribbean. His four voyages began lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.

He went to sea young and sailed as far as the British Isles and West Africa. Based in Lisbon for some years, he made a plan to reach Asia and its spices by sailing west. He thought the Earth was smaller than it is, which made the plan seem possible. Portugal turned him down. After years of lobbying, Isabella I of Castile and Ferdinand II of Aragon agreed to back him in 1492, the year they took Granada.

On his first voyage he landed in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492 and went on to Cuba and Hispaniola (see Columbus reaches the Caribbean). Three more voyages followed, the last ending in 1504, reaching the coasts of South and Central America. He held to the end that he had reached Asia.

As governor of Hispaniola he ruled harshly. The Taíno people were forced to dig for gold and many were enslaved, and in 1500 the crown removed him and sent him home in chains. He died in Spain in 1506, rich but bitter. His voyages started the Columbian Exchange of crops, animals and diseases, and the Spanish empire in America. He is honoured as a discoverer and blamed as the start of conquest, and both views are argued over today.
sum: Christopher Columbus was a navigator from Genoa who sailed west across the Atlantic for the Spanish crown in 1492 and reached the Caribbean. His four voyages began lasting contact between Europe and the Americas.
